newsitem.title: USA: Oshkosh B'Gosh to close plant, sees charge.
newsitem.headline: Oshkosh B'Gosh to close plant, sees charge.

text.p: OshKosh B'Gosh Inc., seeing a dropoff in demand for men's bib overalls while the children's version of the workclothes has gained in popularity, said Thursday it is closing the Oshkosh, Wis., plant where men's overalls are made.

The maker of work clothes and children's apparel said it plans to close the plant in April. It will record a charge of $7.2 million, or 60 cents a share, in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1996 to cover the costs of the closing and a previously announced closing of its Columbia, Ky., plant.

"It is not cost-effective for us to continue manufacturing operations when we are utilizing only one-third of the plant," Michael Wachtel, executive vice president and chief operating officer, said in a statement.
In addition, demand for men's bib overalls is not enough to justify the cost of continuing operations, even if it moves to a smaller building, he said.
In the future, the men's bib overalls currently being manufactured in Oshkosh will be made overseas.
The plant, opened by OshKosh B'Gosh in 1985, employs about 75 people. OshKosh B'Gosh said it is pursuing a buyer for the 91,400 square foot facility.

The write-down of assets will have no impact on the company's cash flow. "OshKosh's financial position remains strong. With over $140 million of net worth, no long-term debt and continued positive cash flow from operations, the company is well-positioned financially for the future," said David Omachinski, OshKosh B'Gosh chief financial officer.

Excluding the Oshkosh facility, OshKosh B'Gosh operates six manufacturing plants and two distribution centres employing over 4,700 people in the United States. Total corporate-wide employment is about 5,200 employees.
